title: Normalized ordinary tensor isomorphism for shifted free modules
statement: Let k be any commutative ring and let S(n) be the actual single free rank-one complex cupSingleModule k n of [lem-sc-module-cup-homology-representability]. For any integers p and q there exists a complex isomorphism i:S(p+q) to S(p) tensor S(q). Under the singleObjXSelf identifications in the three support degrees, i.hom evaluated at 1 equals the (p,q)-summand inclusion of 1 tensor 1. Explicitly, singleObjXSelf(p+q).inv followed by i.hom.f(p+q) applied to 1 equals ιTensorObj S(p) S(q) p q (p+q) applied to singleObjXSelf(p).inv(1) tensor singleObjXSelf(q).inv(1). This is an ordinary tensor of complexes, with no derived localization or arbitrary representative maps.

source.place: Section 15.64, equation-simple-tor-product: the single free complexes and tensor-of-cocycles construction.

proof.text: The ordinary total tensor of S(p) and S(q) has zero terms outside p+q: in every summand other than (p,q), at least one single-complex term is zero. The differential is zero because both single-complex differentials are zero. In degree p+q, the singleObjXSelf maps identify the only summand with k tensor_k k. Multiplication k tensor_k k to k is an isomorphism with inverse a to 1 tensor a. Compose its inverse with the summand inclusion and singleObjXSelf on the source to give the degree-p+q component; give the unique map between zero objects in every other degree. These maps commute with the zero differentials and are degreewise isomorphisms, hence form a complex isomorphism i. Its normalized value at 1 is the displayed inclusion of the transported 1 tensor transported 1. This proof includes all integer degrees and the zero ring; no nontriviality hypothesis is needed.

proof_origin.note: Isolates only the normalized ordinary single-complex isomorphism from the parent; representative-map naturality and derived compatibility are proved in the parent.
